name: Meshullam
overview: The name Meshullam appears multiple times in Scripture, identifying various individuals across different tribes and roles. Notably, Meshullam is recorded as the grandfather of Shaphan, a scribe who served King Josiah (2 Kings 22:3), and as a son of Zerubbabel, linking him to the post-exilic leadership (1 Chronicles 3:19). Other references show Meshullams among the tribes of Gad and Benjamin, including leaders, priests, and those involved in temple service and restoration (1 Chronicles 5:13; 9:7-8). These diverse mentions highlight Meshullam as a name associated with faithful service, leadership, and covenant community in both pre- and post-exilic Israel.
